Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
525 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Hot summer weather continues through the forecast period.  
 
- We'll need to monitor for potential isolated to scattered
  showers/storms near the coast and offshore in the Gulf today.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 AM CDT Sun Aug  2026

Our long awaited "cold" front is pushing through Texas, bringing 
much lower dew points / humidity in its wake. The front has been 
somewhat lagging, with the leading edge just reaching the northern 
fringe of our CWA as of the time of writing this AFD (~12AM CDT). 
The increasingly diffused front is expected to stall near the coast 
and could provide a focal region for convective development. Some of 
the CAMs suggest isolated to scattered activity will develop near 
the coast and offshore during the morning hours. So we'll be keeping 
a watchful eye on the radar just in case. 

Dew points are forecast to drop well down into the 60s for most 
areas north of I-10 this afternoon. We may even see 50s dew points 
in the Brazos Valley. Meanwhile, coastal dew points are forecast to 
remain in the mid/upper 70s. Quite soupy for our beach friends. 
Inland afternoon temperatures are expected to be in the upper 90s, 
with low 90s at the coast. But the highest heat indices may actually 
occur at the coast (104-106) due to the higher humidity. With a 
potential lingering frontal boundary in place, I guess we cannot 
completely rule out an isolated shower or storm along the boundary 
this afternoon. 

The low-levels look to remain dry on Monday, with a similar dew 
point regime as Sunday. Meanwhile, ridging aloft should strengthen, 
warming the overall temperature profile. Therefore, temperatures in 
many spots may be flirting with the 100 degree mark. Ridging aloft 
should increase as the week progresses while deep LL onshore flow 
becomes established thanks to the increasing influence of a sfc high 
well to our east. This combo should keep conditions hot and 
increasingly humid. Perhaps we can lower temps somewhat later in the 
week due to the potential for some increased cumulus as well as 
diurnally influenced isolated shower / thunderstorm activity. But we 
see no real relief from the heat. Tis August in SE TX. 

Self

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance) 
Issued at 525 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

Mainly a wind forecast, but the forecast gets a bit more complex
closer to the coast where interactions with a frontal boundary
looks to bring multiple wind shifts. For the northern terminals
(IAH and northward), anticipating just light northerly winds and
VFR conditions to prevail through the afternoon. Further south,
winds start out light and westerly this morning then becoming
northwesterly in the late morning. This will then be followed by a
shift to southerly winds as the front retreats northward. There is
ongoing scattered showers/storms near Matagorda Bay and offshore 
early this morning. While we can't entirely rule out a rogue 
shower along the coast throughout the day, the potential is too 
low to include any SH/TS mentions in this TAF package.

Winds become light and variable overnight into Monday morning.
It's worth noting that with low-level moisture increasing
overnight, there is at least some potential for reduced 
visibilities due to patchy fog for western areas early Monday 
morning. Uncertainty is a bit too high at the moment though to 
include any mentions of this in this TAF package.

Batiste

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1127 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Gusty southwest winds will gradually decrease overnight into
Sunday morning. A frontal boundary will approach from the north,
stalling and becoming increasingly diffused near the coast. The
front could help spark off a few showers and thunderstorms along
the coast and over the open Gulf. Best chance of a heavier thunderstorm
is offshore. Light west to southwest winds are expected Sunday 
into Monday, followed by light to moderate south winds Tuesday and
Wednesday. Winds may become more southeasterly by the end of the 
week. 

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
643 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A weak frontal boundary will move through the region early
  today, bringing a 20 to 60% chance of rain across central to
  south central Louisiana.

- Some slightly drier air will work into the region today with
  dewpoints falling into the mid to upper 60s in some areas, but
  both high and low temperatures will remain at or above average.

- Isolated diurnally driven afternoon thunderstorms will be
  possible each day through the work week, with rain chances in
  the 15 to 30% range.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Saturday)
Issued at 1218 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

Current conditions across the forecast area are calm but warm,
with temperatures in the lower 80s and dewpoints only a few
degrees lower. The weak frontal boundary expected to move through
the area is currently located just north of the CWA and is
forecast to move through overnight into this morning. As the front
sweeps across the forecast area, isolated to scattered showers and
thunderstorms are expected to develop along and ahead of it,
especially across central to south central Louisiana.

The front is not expected to provide much in the way of
temperature relief, with highs remaining near to slightly above
climatological normals. The "relief" will instead come from the
relatively short lived northerly flow behind the front, which will
help lower dewpoints by around 7 to 12 degrees and consequently
reduce afternoon heat indices. Nevertheless, this will be short
lived, with southerly flow and Gulf moisture making an unwelcome
return on Monday.

For the first half of the workweek, the frontal boundary will
linger near the coast while southerly flow prevails through the
remainder of the week. Aloft, the area will reside between an
upper ridge expanding from the Desert Southwest into the Southern
Plains and an upper low over the SECONUS. Increasing moisture, the
subtle weakness aloft, and daytime heating will support isolated
convection through much of the workweek, moreso across the eastern
half of the CWA. Temperatures will remain slightly above average
and fairly uniform each day. A few locations could approach Heat
Advisory criteria during the workweek; however, area wide heat
hazards appear unlikely at this time.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 630 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

A cool front is moving through the region at this hour. It has
mostly been a dry fropa, but now that the front has met with moist
airmass off of the Gulf there is a widespread area of convection
developing across the Atchafalaya Basin and south. 

This area of disturbing weather will continue moving southeast
into the north Gulf along with the front. Thus, not anticipating
very much impact from these storms at terminals today. Only
Acadiana will see scattered showers and storms through roughly
13z, they will clear thereafter. 

Elsewhere, expected mostly clear to clearing skies with VFR
conditions and northwest winds in the 5 to 7 knot range through
sundown. Winds will diminish with sundown with the return of high
pressure aloft. 

11/Calhoun

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1218 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

A weak frontal boundary will move across the coastal waters
through tonight into Sunday morning, tightening the pressure
gradient over the coastal waters. This has resulted in elevated
southwesterly winds and will continue to support isolated to
scattered convection. With sustained winds of 15 to 20 knots and
gusts up to 25 knots, a Small Craft Advisory remains in effect
through late this morning. Light southerly flow will become
reestablished Monday and persist through the remainder of the
week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1218 AM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

Rain chances will increase across central to south central
Louisiana early today as a weak frontal boundary approaches the
area. A brief period of northerly to northwesterly winds can be
expected behind the front, bringing some slightly drier air into
the region. Minimum afternoon RH values today and Monday are
expected to range from 35 to 50 percent. Winds will turn back out
of the south on Monday. Isolated afternoon thunderstorms will be
possible through much of the workweek.

&&

.LCH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
LA...None.
TX...None.
GM...Small Craft Advisory until 10 AM CDT this morning for GMZ450-452-
     455-470-472-475.

&&

$$
